parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the prompt as a black-box pure-std Rust 2021 port requiring Cargo structure, root test12.rs, argv[1] default behavior, exact line order, and byte-for-byte output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership but spawned probe_matrix and probe_unicode children, with a nested probe helper also spawned; children performed probes and some also wrote implementations into /output.
parallel.implementation: The final implementation used root test12.rs plus idna modules implementing simple xn-- prefixing, one-prefix stripping, ASCII-only lowercase normalization, nonempty validity, ASCII/IDN checks, TLD extraction, and dot counting.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The shared /output tree accumulated parent and child project layouts; the parent inspected extra files, deleted duplicate lib/inspect artifacts, rebuilt, and delivered Cargo.toml, test12.rs, idna modules, and executable.
parallel.verification: The parent ran cargo build, rustc builds, default-output comparison, and broader byte-for-byte comparisons against /workspace/dataset/test12_executable after cleanup; official evaluation passed 40/40.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No final functional defect is evidenced, but one child was interrupted after waits and overlapping child writes forced a cleanup/rebuild cycle before closure.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same black-box port requirements, including pure std, root test12.rs, Cargo project, exact output, and probing the provided executable instead of reading library sources.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, behavior inference, implementation, packaging, verification, and final response with multi-agent disabled and no child activity.
serial.implementation: It implemented a cohesive src/lib.rs and src/idna module layout with ASCII helper logic and a root test12.rs entry that called the inferred functions in the C++ output order.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial project was assembled once into a stable Cargo layout with root test12.rs, src/lib.rs, src/idna/mod.rs, src/idna/ascii.rs, release target, and /output/test12 executable.
serial.verification: It ran cargo test, cargo build --release, rustc --edition=2021 test12.rs -O -o test12, and byte-for-byte comparisons across samples and edge cases; official evaluation passed 40/40.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved defect or incomplete required step is visible at closure, and no subagent result or shared-write reconciliation remained.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the 12 printed API results, pure Rust 2021, no crates, root test12.rs, Cargo support, and black-box executable probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same requirements and used the executable as behavioral oracle for exact output and edge cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference; both aligned on the simplified mock-IDNA semantics and passed all official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split behavior probing to children while the parent also implemented and integrated; four subagent threads existed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, implementation, integration, and verification in one owner with multi-agent disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced overlapping owners for probing and implementation artifacts; serial avoided cross-agent ownership boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children received delegated probe tasks through encrypted briefs and independently inferred behavior; one completed result returned and another child was interrupted after writing and testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The same agent retained all context from probes through implementation, so there were no cross-agent handoffs or interface assumptions to adjudicate.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra handoff and shared-workspace boundaries, but no evidenced missing requirement in a child brief caused unusable final behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent and children independently wrote project files under /output; the final parent-normalized tree used root idna modules and matched observed behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one src-based project in a single apply_patch and kept that structure through compilation and delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementations encoded the same behavior, but parallel had redundant source/layout edits from multiple agents while serial had a single coherent edit path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited for child results, received the probe_matrix final report, timed out waiting on probe_unicode, interrupted it, then inspected the shared tree and continued.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no child result lifecycle; local probing and verification fed directly into implementation and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred result waiting and interruption overhead, but it did not leave required final functionality unjoined or unverified.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Shared /output writes produced duplicate helper files and overlapping source/config edits that the parent had to inspect, delete, and rebuild around.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one stable workspace layout with no subagent writes, no duplicate helper files, and no merge cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the material process difference: parallel shared-state collision created cleanup work; serial integration stayed linear.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built with cargo and rustc, compared default and broad edge-case outputs before and after cleanup, and official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran unit tests, release build, rustc output, a compare script across many cases, and official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both supplied strong acceptance evidence; serial added cargo test, while parallel added post-cleanup rebuild and comparison after shared-write reconciliation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent more time and requests, waited on children, interrupted one running child, cleaned duplicate files, and still closed with a passing artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed faster with fewer tool calls and no child wait/interrupt cycle, then closed after successful local and official verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel coordination added overhead and cleanup but did not exhaust the budget or impair the final solution; serial was simpler and shorter.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current evaluations are concordant: both parallel and serial completed and passed 40 of 40 testcases. Both inferred the same shallow executable behavior and delivered a compiling Rust project. The concrete process difference is that the parallel run used children that also wrote overlapping project files, requiring parent cleanup and rebuild, while the serial run used a single coherent owner and avoided merge cleanup.
parallel_contributors: Parallel probing by parent and children produced enough behavior coverage to implement the mock IDNA functions.
The parent corrected the shared-output collision by inspecting duplicate files, deleting extras, rebuilding, and rechecking outputs.
serial_contributors: The serial agent performed black-box probing and implementation in one context.
Serial validation included cargo test, cargo build, rustc, and byte-for-byte comparisons before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two final project layouts differed, with parallel using root idna modules and serial using src/idna modules, but both layouts satisfied the prompt and official tests.
No ordinary coding defect explains an outcome gap because there is no outcome gap.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel process cost only
